subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: What trusted sender identity contract should OpenClaw publish for inbound messages: a stable identityLinks-derived principal, an operator-attested sender field, a human display name, or no trusted sender identity for now?
rationale: The code already intentionally keeps human names out of trusted system metadata, and the related PRs prove multiple plausible shapes with different security, privacy, and compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Approve A Canonical Principal
options.body: Publish one stable principal/canonical-id field derived only from trusted platform ids or configured identity links, and keep display names in untrusted context unless separately approved.

options.title: Accept Trusted Display Names
options.body: Allow a platform-resolved display-name field in trusted metadata, but require explicit privacy, spoofing, redaction, and compatibility rules before implementation.

options.title: Keep Current Boundary
options.body: Do not add a trusted sender identity field yet; keep current untrusted sender context and agent registry workarounds until the identity model is redesigned.

recommendation.title: Approve A Canonical Principal
recommendation.body: Publish one stable principal/canonical-id field derived only from trusted platform ids or configured identity links, and keep display names in untrusted context unless separately approved.
